legend: Four images from the same case. Occasional stripped, elongated spindle nuclei and a platelet clot in bloody background that requires imaging correlation to suggest a haemangioma (Giemsa) (shown here). A tissue fragment of poorly defined spindle cells and collagenous stroma (Giemsa) (Fig. <<36372>>). Core biopsy of liver showing fatty change (12 to 6 o’clock) and cores of vascular tumour with irregular, often dilated, thin-walled vessels separated by collagenous stroma with spindle cells (core biopsy, H&E) (Fig. <<36373>>). Irregular, thin-walled, variably dilated blood vessels separated by paucicellular collagen tissue of haemangioma (core biopsy, H&E) (Fig. <<36374>>).

MRI of a mass in the right vastus medialis.
A minute tissue fragment suggestive of a thin vessel, consisting of bland spindle cells (Giemsa).
A moderately cellular tissue fragment of spindle cells, with no definite vessel formation (Giemsa).
Collections of capillaries and slightly more open small vessels in the interstitium between skeletal muscle fibres and occasional degenerate small muscle fibres (H&E).
MRI of a mass in the soft tissue of the shoulder.
A tissue fragment of collagen and spindle cells, as well as a more cellular area where the orientation of the spindle cells suggests small vessels (Giemsa).

Collection of small vessels, some resembling capillaries, with a range of more dilated, irregular, thin-walled vessels separated by paucicellular collagen and occasional residual skeletal muscle strands (CNB, H&E).
